extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners, patent applicants, and practitioners (agents/attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the required parts, form, content, and examination practice for U.S. patent applications, including drawings, detailed description, best mode, claim form/numbering, dependent and multiple dependent claims, and related fee/processing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of drawings matching specification
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Patent Application Processing (OPAP) will review the specification, including the brief description, to determine whether all figures of drawings described in the specification are present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the specification describes a figure not present in the drawings (or lacks drawings), the application will be treated according to the applicable MPEP provision (e.g., MPEP § 601.01(g) or § 601.01(f) depending on filing date and application type). The examiner should object where the brief description of drawings does not correctly describe all figures (example: drawings show Figures 1A, 1B, 1C but brief description only refers to Figure 1) and require applicant to provide a correct brief description of each figure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for drawings (37 CFR 1.84): black ink vs color
rubrics_metrics.description: Black and white drawings are normally required (India ink or equivalent for solid black lines). Color drawings are permitted in design applications and, on rare occasions, in utility applications only with petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Color drawings must be reproducible in black and white for printed patent; international (PCT) applications do not permit color drawings (PCT Rule 11.13). Petitions to accept color drawings in utility applications must include the fee (§ 1.17(h)), one set of color drawings if filed electronically (three sets if not), and an amendment to the specification inserting specified language as first paragraph of the brief description of the drawings indicating file contains at least one color drawing and that copies with color drawings will be provided upon request and fee payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs: when acceptable and quality requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs (including photocopies) are not ordinarily permitted but will be accepted when photographs are the only practicable medium to illustrate the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples where photographs are acceptable: electrophoresis gels, blots, autoradiographs, cell cultures, histological sections, animals, plants, in vivo imaging, TLC plates, crystalline structures, and ornamental effects in design applications. If the subject admits of illustration by a drawing, the examiner may require a drawing instead. Photographs must be of sufficient quality so all details are reproducible in the printed patent. Color photographs are accepted only if the conditions for color drawings (see 37 CFR 1.84(a)(2)) and black & white photograph criteria are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed description requirement (enablement and written description)
rubrics_metrics.description: The detailed description required by 37 CFR 1.71 must be in such particularity as to enable a person skilled in the art to make and use the invention without extensive experimentation and must clearly convey enough information to show the applicant invented the claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may use their own terminology if understandable; examiner may require necessary grammatical corrections but not perfect grammar. Reference characters must be applied properly (no single reference used for two different parts or for a part and its modification; see 37 CFR 1.84(p)). Every feature in the claims should be illustrated, and there should be no superfluous illustrations. The description functions as a 'dictionary' for the claims and must provide clear support/antecedent basis for all terms used in the claims. Cross-references: 37 CFR 1.71, MPEP §§ 608.01, 2161, 2162, 608.01(i),(o), § 1302.01, § 2111.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best mode disclosure (35 U.S.C. 112)
rubrics_metrics.description: The best mode contemplated by the inventor for carrying out the invention must be set forth in the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no statutory requirement to disclose a specific example. Absence of a specific working example is not necessarily evidence of failure to disclose best mode; only evidence of concealment (accidental or intentional) is relevant in evaluating adequacy. A defect in best mode at filing cannot be cured by post-filing amendment that adds the best mode (such an amendment may be treated as new matter). See MPEP § 2165–2165.04 for discussion and case citations (Spectra-Physics, In re Hay, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory requirement of claims (35 U.S.C. 112)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must conclude with a claim particularly pointing out and distinctly claiming the subject matter which the applicant regards as the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims are the definition of the protection granted; this statutory requirement underlies claim examination and rejections/objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple claims allowed but must differ and not be unduly multiplied
rubrics_metrics.description: More than one claim may be presented provided they differ substantially from each other and are not unduly multiplied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims must meaningfully differ; avoid presenting numerous redundant variations. Fee consequences may apply for excess claims (see §§1.16, § 714.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claims: form and limitations (including multiple dependent claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: One or more claims may be presented in dependent form, referring back to and further limiting another claim; a multiple dependent claim that refers to more than one other claim must refer to such claims in the alternative only and shall not serve as a basis for any other multiple dependent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For fee calculation purposes, a multiple dependent claim is considered to be the number of claims to which direct reference is made. Any claim depending from a multiple dependent claim is considered likewise. Multiple dependent claims must be alternative (e.g., 'according to claims 3 or 4'); cumulative claiming ('claims 3 and 4') is improper. A multiple dependent claim may not refer to claims of different sets (e.g., cannot mix apparatus and process claim sets). If a multiple dependent claim depends from another multiple dependent claim, it should be objected to. See 35 U.S.C. 112(e) and 37 CFR 1.75(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must conform to the specification and have antecedent basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must conform to the invention as set forth in the remainder of the specification and the terms and phrases used in the claims must find clear support or antecedent basis in the description so that their meaning may be ascertained by reference to the description (see § 1.58(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where subject matter not shown in drawing or description is claimed, but the original claim itself constitutes a clear disclosure, the claim should not be objected to merely because drawing/description lack that subject matter; rather the drawing/description should be amended to show it. However, if the claim does not provide its own descriptive disclosure and the subject matter is not shown/described, reject under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) for inadequate written description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended claim structure for improvement-type inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the nature of the case admits (e.g., an improvement), any independent claim should contain, in order: (1) a preamble listing conventional/known elements or steps; (2) a phrase such as 'wherein the improvement comprises,' and (3) the elements/steps/relationships constituting the new or improved portion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ordering helps clarify what is conventional versus claimed improvement; follow as appropriate for improvement claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim numbering preservation (37 CFR 1.126)
rubrics_metrics.description: The original numbering of the claims must be preserved throughout prosecution; canceled claims' numbers are not renumbered; when claims are added they must be numbered consecutively beginning with the number next following the highest numbered claim previously presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When application is ready for allowance, the examiner may renumber claims consecutively in the order they appear or as requested. Use form paragraph 6.17 to notify applicant of numbering issues. In a single-claim case, the claim is not numbered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must commence on a separate sheet/page
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim(s) must commence on a separate physical sheet or electronic page and any sheet including a claim or portion thereof may not contain other parts of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 6.18.01 to object to placement of claims. This follows 37 CFR 1.52(b)(3) and 1.75(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim formatting and punctuation conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each claim should be the object of a sentence starting with 'I (or we) claim,' 'The invention claimed is' (or equivalent), begin with a capital letter and end with a period; periods may not be used elsewhere except for abbreviations. Where a claim sets forth plurality of elements/steps, each element/step should be separated by a line indentation (37 CFR 1.75(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference characters corresponding to elements may be used in claims but should be enclosed in parentheses to avoid confusion. There may be plural indentations to segregate subcombinations. Printing limitations may alter complex formats. Examiners may object to claims with crowded lines (use form paragraph 7.29.03) or missing parentheses around reference characters (7.29.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement of claims to facilitate examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims should preferably be arranged in order of scope with the least restrictive claim presented first; dependent claims should be grouped with the claim(s) to which they refer; separate species, product and process claims should be grouped where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such arrangements facilitate classification and examination. Presenting claims by scope and grouping like claims reduces prosecution difficulties post-final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate claims practice
rubrics_metrics.description: When two claims comply with 35 U.S.C. 112(d) but are duplicates or so close that they cover the same thing, it is proper after allowing one claim to object to the other as being a substantial duplicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.05.05 to warn of duplicate claims (if not allowable) and 7.05.06 to object when duplicate. Examiner notes: give applicant opportunity to correct; if claims are allowable, use different paragraph. Dependent claims that do not specify a further limitation should be rejected with form paragraphs 7.36 and 7.36.01 rather than merely warned as duplicates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner handling of claims referring to numerically following claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If dependent claims refer to numerically succeeding claims, examiners should object and not treat such claims on the merits if the reference cannot be understood; however, if dependency is clear (as presented and as it will be renumbered for issue), all claims should be examined on the merits and an examiner's amendment prepared if order changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring unusual problems to supervisor. Examples provided showing when to object (Example A) and when to examine and renumber (Example B). Ensure each Office action explicitly states what rejection/objection/requirement applies to each claim embodiment as required by 35 U.S.C. 132.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification practice for embodiments in multiple dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When referring to embodiments included in multiple dependent claims, identify each embodiment by claim numbers involved (starting with highest) as needed; when all embodiments are subject to a common rejection/objection, reference may be made only to the dependent claim number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table illustrates approved practice for identifying claims and embodiments. Follow guidance (A),(B),(C) in examiner practice for clarity in Office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling and processing responsibilities for multiple dependent claims (OPAP, TC, Examiner)
rubrics_metrics.description: OPAP verifies whether multiple dependent claims filed with the application are in proper alternative form and calculates filing fee implications; Technology Center (TC) technical support verifies compliance with statute/rules for multiple dependent claims added by amendment and calculates additional fees; examiners follow statutory rules in treating multiple dependent claims and object to improper forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPAP uses form PTO/SB/07 in conjunction with PTO/SB/06 for fee calculation; TC staff will place PTO/SB/07 in file when multiple dependent claims are added later. If multiple dependent claim added without proper fee, amendment should not be entered until fee received; applicant should be contacted to pay additional fee; include copy of fee calculation form when notifying applicant of insufficient fee. If TC notes improper reference in added/amended multiple dependent claim, indicate by encircling numeral '1' in 'Dep. Claim' column on PTO/SB/07 to call examiner attention. Examiner must treat each claim embodiment individually (all claims should be examined).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee computation rules for multiple dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Use form PTO/SB/07 with PTO/SB/06 to compute fees. A proper multiple dependent claim is considered to be that number of dependent claims to which it refers for fee calculation; an improper multiple dependent claim generally triggers only a single objection and is counted as one dependent claim for fee accounting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If none of the multiple dependent claims is proper, the multiple dependent claim fee (37 CFR 1.16(j)) will not be required. If at least one multiple dependent claim is proper, the fee is required. OPAP may mark improper multiple dependent claims with encircled '1' in Dep. Claims column. Any claim depending from an improper multiple dependent claim is also considered improper and counted as one dependent claim. A sample fee calculation example is provided in the MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to claims must comply with 37 CFR 1.121(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment to the claims must be made in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should ensure amendments entered into the record conform to rules on presentation and entry of amendments; review for new matter, proper format, and fee compliance when amendments add multiple dependent claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference characters usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference characters must be properly applied; no single reference character should be used for two different parts or for a given part and its modification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.84(p). Reference characters used in claims should be enclosed within parentheses to avoid confusion (object if not enclosed — form paragraph 7.29.02). Improper use may render claim indefinite; if so, use form paragraph 7.34.01 to reject under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) rather than just pointing out minor informalities.
